title: Trial of Self-Applied Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation for Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy
official: Single-Arm Bayesian Phase II Trial of Self-Applied Transcutaneous Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation for Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy
summary: This purpose of this study is to evaluate whether transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) improves chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) symptoms by assessing changes in daily symptom trajectories following treatment initiation. The study will also examine potential mechanisms of action through longitudinal assessment of inflammatory biomarkers, corticospinal excitability, and autonomic nervous system function.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Age 18-80 years
2. Prior exposure to platinum, taxane, or vinca alkaloid chemotherapy
3. Glove/stocking dysesthesias ≥3 months that began after neurotoxic chemotherapy
4. Worst CIPN-related symptom ≥4/10 over the last week

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Unstable cardiac disease/Known arrhythmias
2. Head or neck cancer or metastases
3. Recent ear trauma or active dermatologic disease at the stimulation site
4. \<2 months since completion of cancer treatment or surgery (i.e, tumor resection, radiation therapy, and/or taxane/platinum/vinca alkaloid chemotherapy treatments. Maintenance therapies, including hormonal therapy or Poly (ADP-ribose) Polymerase (PARP) inhibitors, are allowed and not part of exclusion criteria. Patients may have pending reconstructive surgeries planned as long as it is planned outside of the study participation window.)
5. Metal implants in the head or neck (e.g., cochlear implant)
6. Implanted electronic or magnetic devices (e.g., pacemaker, medication pumps, other implanted neurostimulation systems)
7. Known allergy to tape/adhesives
8. History of seizure/epilepsy, intracranial pathology, or other neurological condition associated with increased seizure risk
9. Pregnancy or actively breast feeding
